title: Invertibility propagates to the localizing closure
statement:
Let $\mathcal T,\mathcal T'$ be triangulated categories with arbitrary direct
sums, let $\mathcal S\subset\mathcal T$ be a class of objects, and let
$\Loc(\mathcal S)$ be the smallest full triangulated subcategory of
$\mathcal T$ containing $\mathcal S$ and closed under arbitrary direct sums.
Let $F_1,F_2:\mathcal T\to\mathcal T'$ (or $\Loc(\mathcal S)\to\mathcal T'$)
be exact functors preserving direct sums and $\eta:F_1\to F_2$ a natural
transformation of exact functors, i.e. compatible with the shift
isomorphisms. Then the full subcategory

$$
\mathcal C_\eta=\{K\ :\ \eta_K\text{ is an isomorphism}\}
$$

is a triangulated subcategory closed under arbitrary direct sums (and under
direct summands). Consequently, if $\mathcal S\subset\mathcal C_\eta$, then
$\Loc(\mathcal S)\subset\mathcal C_\eta$.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal D$ for the common domain of $F_1,F_2$: either $\mathcal T$ or $\Loc(\mathcal S)$. All objects at which $\eta$ is evaluated lie in $\mathcal D$. The full subcategory $\mathcal C_\eta$ is replete: for $u:K\xrightarrow{\sim}L$, naturality gives $\eta_L=F_2(u)\eta_KF_1(u)^{-1}$; hence invertibility is unchanged by replacing an object by an isomorphic one. It contains zero: exact functors are additive, so $1_{F_a(0)}=F_a(1_0)=F_a(0)=0$. Consequently $F_a(0)$ is a zero object, and the unique map $\eta_0$ between these two zero objects is invertible.

source.place: Preliminary zero/repleteness checks for the full isomorphism locus; Stacks Tag 0145 (derived-definition-triangulated-category) and Tag 014V (derived-definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories).

proof.text: Let $c_{a,K}:F_a(K[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}F_a(K)[1]$ be the specified shift isomorphisms. The assumed shift compatibility is $c_{2,K}\eta_{K[1]}=\eta_K[1]c_{1,K}$, so $\eta_{K[1]}=c_{2,K}^{-1}\eta_K[1]c_{1,K}$. If $\eta_K$ has inverse $\beta_K$, the displayed conjugate has inverse $c_{1,K}^{-1}\beta_K[1]c_{2,K}$. Conversely the same formula makes $\eta_K[1]$ invertible if $\eta_{K[1]}$ is; applying the inverse shift then makes $\eta_K$ invertible. Thus $K\in\mathcal C_\eta$ if and only if $K[1]\in\mathcal C_\eta$. Apply this equivalence to $K[-1]$ and iterate to obtain stability under every integer shift.

source.place: Shifts paragraph; Stacks Tag 014V and the following definition of a shift-compatible 2-morphism.

proof.text: For a distinguished triangle $K\xrightarrow{u}L\xrightarrow{v}M\xrightarrow{w}K[1]$ in $\mathcal D$, apply [lem-sf-triangle-two-out-of-three] to $F_1,F_2,\eta$. Its hypotheses are precisely the exactness and stated shift compatibility here: the image triangles are distinguished, naturality gives their first two squares, and their connecting square is the identity $c_{2,K}F_2(w)\eta_M=c_{2,K}\eta_{K[1]}F_1(w)=\eta_K[1]c_{1,K}F_1(w)$. Therefore invertibility on any two vertices implies invertibility on the third. Together with zero, repleteness and all shifts from Steps 1-2, this meets the criterion in [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], including the case with first and third vertices in the subcategory. Hence $\mathcal C_\eta$ is triangulated, with the induced distinguished triangles.

source.place: Cones paragraph; Stacks Tag 014A (derived-lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle) and Tag 05QM (derived-definition-triangulated-subcategory).

proof.text: Let $(K_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I}$ be any small family in $\mathcal C_\eta$, put $K=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}K_\alpha$, and write $i_\alpha:K_\alpha\to K$ for its inclusions. Preservation of this coproduct means that $(F_a(K),F_a(i_\alpha))$ is a coproduct cocone. Using the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] for the discrete small category $I$, define $\beta:F_2(K)\to F_1(K)$ uniquely by $\beta F_2(i_\alpha)=F_1(i_\alpha)\eta_{K_\alpha}^{-1}$. Naturality gives $(\beta\eta_K)F_1(i_\alpha)=F_1(i_\alpha)$ and $(\eta_K\beta)F_2(i_\alpha)=F_2(i_\alpha)$ for every $\alpha$. Coproduct uniqueness yields $\beta\eta_K=1$ and $\eta_K\beta=1$. Thus $K\in\mathcal C_\eta$. This argument also covers the empty family; no exactness of arbitrary sums of triangles is used.

source.place: Direct sums paragraph, expanded by the defining universal property; Stacks Tag 002F (categories-definition-colimit).

proof.text: Suppose $i:K\to L$ and $p:L\to K$ are morphisms in $\mathcal D$ with $pi=1_K$, and $\eta_L$ is invertible. Set $\beta_K=F_1(p)\eta_L^{-1}F_2(i)$. Naturality for $i$ and $p$ gives $\beta_K\eta_K=F_1(p)\eta_L^{-1}\eta_LF_1(i)=1$ and $\eta_K\beta_K=F_2(p)\eta_L\eta_L^{-1}F_2(i)=1$. Thus $\mathcal C_\eta$ is closed under retracts in its domain, in particular under direct summands: for $L=K\oplus K'$ use the canonical inclusion and projection, and repeat for $K'$. This explicitly proves the summands assertion rather than using the proof, or the counterexample clause, of the generating-class lemma.

source.place: Summands paragraph: explicit inclusion/projection inverse calculation.

proof.text: Assume $\mathcal S\subset\mathcal C_\eta$. If $\mathcal D=\mathcal T$, Steps 1-4 show that $\mathcal C_\eta$ is one of the full replete triangulated subcategories closed under small coproducts and containing $\mathcal S$; the defining minimality of $\Loc(\mathcal S)$ therefore gives $\Loc(\mathcal S)\subset\mathcal C_\eta$. If $\mathcal D=\Loc(\mathcal S)$, its triangulated structure is induced from $\mathcal T$ by [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory], and its coproducts are ambient ones: their objects lie in $\mathcal D$ by its defining closure, and the ambient universal property still holds after restricting test objects to this full subcategory. To check closure as a subcategory of $\mathcal T$, take a distinguished triangle in $\mathcal T$ whose first and third vertices lie in $\mathcal C_\eta$; the middle vertex is isomorphic to an object of $\mathcal D$ by the full-subcategory criterion, and repleteness puts it in $\mathcal D$. Transport the triangle across that isomorphism, apply Step 3 in $\mathcal D$, and use repleteness again to put the original middle vertex in $\mathcal C_\eta$. Thus $\mathcal C_\eta$ is a full replete triangulated subcategory of $\mathcal T$ closed under its small coproducts. The same minimality gives $\Loc(\mathcal S)\subset\mathcal C_\eta$ in this case as well. This is a consequence of the general localizing-closure definition in the statement; the constructible-complex specialization is downstream and is not used as an input.

source.place: Conclusion paragraph, both choices of functor domain; Stacks Tag 05QM and Tag 002F for inherited structures.

lean.statement: theorem isoLocus_localizing {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} C] [Category.{v₂} D] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] [IsTriangulated C] [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D] [IsTriangulated D] [HasCoproducts.{w} C] [HasCoproducts.{w} D] (S : ObjectProperty C) (F₁ F₂ : C ⥤ D) [F₁.CommShift ℤ] [F₂.CommShift ℤ] [F₁.IsTriangulated] [F₂.IsTriangulated] [∀ I : Type w, PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) F₁] [∀ I : Type w, PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) F₂] (η : F₁ ⟶ F₂) [NatTrans.CommShift η ℤ] : η.isoLocus.IsTriangulated ∧ (∀ I : Type w, Nonempty (η.isoLocus.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (Discrete I))) ∧ Nonempty η.isoLocus.IsStableUnderRetracts ∧ (S ≤ η.isoLocus → sInf {P : ObjectProperty C | S ≤ P ∧ P.IsTriangulated ∧ ∀ I : Type w, Nonempty (P.IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape (Discrete I))} ≤ η.isoLocus)
lean.note: Uses the existing upstream NatTrans.isoLocus. The localizing closure of the arbitrary object class S is expanded as its defining sInf of triangulated, coproduct-closed object properties; no new closure definition or specialized derived-category prerequisite is introduced. IsClosedUnderColimitsOfShape includes arbitrary coproduct cocones, and hence isomorphism closure by singleton coproducts. The abstract source category also permits taking the source itself to be Loc(S).
